answer: Because the thread collateral is checked against the sable claim at intake, the falcon audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. Posted collateral must equal 7 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases therefore has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
